newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU renews sanctions on Nigeria.
newsitem.headline: EU renews sanctions on Nigeria.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers on Monday extended for another six months EU sanctions on Nigeria imposed over human rights abuses.
The decision was taken without discussion at a ministerial meeting in Brussels.

"The general human rights situation and the pace and the manner of the transition to civil democratic rule (in Nigeria) continue to give rise to serious concern," the ministers said in a document accompanying their decision.
EU sanctions on Nigeria consist mainly of restrictions on travel to the EU by Nigerian officials and military personnel. They were due to expire in early December.
The document said that while there had been "some modest steps in the right direction, there was not sufficient evidence of progress to modify the EU position regarding Nigeria."

Africa's most populous nation has been sharply criticised around the world for alleged human rights abuses and last year's hanging of nine minority rights activists from the Ogoni tribe, including writer Ken Saro-Wiwa.
It unexpectedly freed three opposition activists last week as part of its attempts to return to the Commonwealth, the club of Britain and its former colonies, from which it was suspended last year.
Other government opponents remain in detention, however, including Moshood Abiola, the businessman presumed to have won a 1993 presidential vote.
